intro: These aren't therapy, and your brain deserves real support when things get heavy. Your school's counseling center is a good place, and 988 is always there. These cards are for the everyday spirals, the ones a friend could talk you out of.

cards.back: Behind compared to what? Name one real deadline. Make a plan for that one, not the imaginary ones.
You're comparing your inside to their highlight reel. Text one friend and ask how they're really doing. Watch the myth fall apart.

cards.front: "If I fail this, everything falls apart."
cards.back: Play it forward for real. What would happen next? And after that? There's a next step on the other side of almost everything.
Write down the worst case, the best case, and the most likely case. Your brain only offered you the first one.
Did you though? List what you did do. Eating, showing up, and answering that one email all count. The day had more in it than the miss.
You can't grade your own mind reading. If it matters, ask them. If it doesn't, let it go.
Count how many times "should" showed up in your head today. Trade one of them for "could" and notice how different the sentence feels.
Find 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell, 1 you can taste. Your body goes first, your thoughts will follow.
Give it an appointment. Ten minutes, later today, fully yours to worry in. If it still matters when the appointment comes, deal with it then. It usually shrinks on the way.
Stressed is a blanket word. Is it tired? Nervous? Lonely? Behind on one specific thing? Naming it makes it smaller and tells you what it needs.
Always? Find one time you didn't. One is enough to break an always.
No major conclusions about your life after 11pm. Write the thought down and let morning you review it. Morning you is much more reasonable.
Can't do all of it, or can't do all of it right now? Pick the smallest piece and do that one. The rest can stay in line.

cards.front: Replaying that awkward thing you said.
cards.back: Nobody is thinking about it as much as you are. They're busy replaying their own. Be as kind to yourself as you would be to them.

cards.front: The to-do list that reads like one giant task.
cards.back: Cover everything except the top line. One thing at a time is the whole plan.
Starting at 8pm still beats starting tomorrow. A messy 30 minutes counts.
Their mood could be a hundred things, and most of them have nothing to do with you. Wait a day before writing the story.

cards.front: "I should be able to handle this alone."
cards.back: Says who? Borrowing a little help is how most people handle most things. Ask the question. Send the text.
Flip a coin. You don't have to obey it. Notice which side you were hoping for while it was in the air. That's your answer.

cards.front: A bad morning becoming "a bad day."
cards.back: Days come in pieces. A rough 9am doesn't get to claim your 2pm. Restart at the next meal.

cards.front: Shallow breathing, shoulders at your ears.
cards.back: In for 4, hold for 4, out for 6. Three rounds. The longer exhale tells your body the emergency is over.
They saw a person try something. That reads braver from the outside than it feels from the inside.
That's double homework. You're allowed to feel it without grading it.
Write down the one Monday thing making the whole week look heavy. It's usually one thing wearing the costume of seven.
